sub_questions.question: Is there a way to test what the knowledge base will retrieve before plugging it into a live app?

claims.claim: The customer can open their dataset and use the Hit Testing panel to test retrieval.
claims.guide_evidence: the **Hit Testing** / retrieval-test panel on the dataset page lets a builder type a sample query

claims.claim: Typing a sample query shows exactly which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores.
claims.guide_evidence: see exactly which chunks would be retrieved and their similarity scores

claims.claim: Hit Testing works without needing to run the full app.
claims.guide_evidence: without needing to run the full app

claims.claim: Hit Testing is a good way to sanity-check chunking and indexing choices before wiring the dataset into a retrieval node.
claims.guide_evidence: Before publishing an app that uses a dataset, the **Hit Testing** / retrieval-test panel on the dataset page lets a builder type a sample query and see exactly which chunks would be retrieved

claims.claim: Hit Testing keeps a history of recent test queries so you can compare runs side by side.

evaluation.rationale: The core answer (use the Hit Testing panel on the dataset page to preview retrieved chunks and similarity scores) is fully grounded in the guide. The final sentence claims Hit Testing keeps a history of recent queries for side-by-side comparison, which the guide never mentions. It is a harmless but unsupported technical detail, so severity is minor.
